title: Technological Risk Assessment of a Breakwater-Protected Offshore Floating Photovoltaic System Across Three European Sea Basins
content: Offshore floating photovoltaic (FPV) systems face significant technological risks associated with extreme environmental loading, structural durability, system maturity and end-of-life management. This study develops and applies a site-specific technological risk-assessment framework to the HEU funded SUREWAVE project, which integrates interconnected FPV modules with a protective floating-breakwater system. Nineteen technological risks were evaluated for one-unit and split-unit configurations at representative Baltic Sea, Mediterranean Sea and North Sea sites. The methodology combines expert elicitation, severity-likelihood risk matrices, numerical hydrodynamic analysis and evidence from component and wave-basin testing. The assessment identifies FPV hinge failure and full-system hydrodynamic survivability as the most significant risks, with the North Sea presenting the highest overall risk profile and the Baltic Sea the lowest. The principal mitigation measure was the introduction of a full-width generation-v3 hinge, which increased the estimated axial ultimate-limit-state capacity from 14 kN for the paired generation-v2 configuration to 37 kN. Numerical simulations of 50-year sea states showed that the revised design reduced maximum predicted hinge loads from 45 to 34 kN at the Baltic site, from 43 to 33 kN in the Mediterranean and from 54 to 40 kN in the North Sea. The updated hinge therefore remained within the estimated axial capacity for the Baltic and Mediterranean cases, while the North Sea maximum exceeded it by approximately 8%, indicating a need for further design refinement and full-scale validation. Most remaining risks were assessed as manageable through proven mooring technology, marine-grade materials, modular construction, monitoring and preventive maintenance. Circularity was evaluated as a cross-cutting consideration covering material recyclability, infrastructure reuse and end-of-life management. The results support the current TRL 5 assessment and provide an evidence-based framework for prioritising component qualification, site selection and further open-sea demonstration of breakwater-protected offshore FPV systems.
